title: Jewels and Stones

concept.title: A set as a quick filter
body: A set is a fast **membership test**. Put the letters that count as jewels into a set. Then look at every stone and test whether its letter is in that set. This is a one-line filter in every language.
Letters are case sensitive here: `a` and `A` are different kinds of stone. For a small fixed alphabet an array of flags would be as fast, but the set works for any kind of key.

statement: The letters in the first word are the types of stones that are jewels. The second word lists the stones you have, one letter per stone. Count how many of your stones are jewels. Upper and lower case letters are different types.
inputFormat: The first line has the word `jewels`.
The second line has the word `stones`.
outputFormat: Print the number of stones that are jewels.
constraints: The words contain lowercase and uppercase English letters.
The letters of the first word are all different.

examples.note: Three stones (a, A, A) are jewels.

hints: Put the jewel letters into a set.
Check every stone against the set.
Count the stones that are found.

starter.python:
jewels = input().strip()
stones = input().strip()

# Your code here

explanation: The jewel letters go into a hash set; every stone is tested against it in O(1).

code.python:
jewels = input().strip()
stones = input().strip()

jewelSet = set(jewels)
count = 0
for stone in stones:
    if stone in jewelSet:
        count += 1
print(count)
